The cost is negligible for constrained infrastructure: it is a CPU evaluation library with an optional GPU path that fits trivially in 24 GB, plus implementation complexity in adapting existing pipelines to the new API and validating the GPU variant's small approximation error. Failure modes include mis-ranking detectors if AutoVUS's random-baseline buffer selection behaves unexpectedly on datasets with unusual anomaly-length distributions, silent divergence of the approximate GPU path beyond its tested error bound, and wasted effort if the reader's production systems do not perform time series anomaly detection at all. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Time Series Foundation Models on the Edge
item.description: Replaces full recomputation or linearly growing KV caches at each forecast refresh with a persistent fixed-size recurrent state for causal time series foundation models, verified equivalent to full recomputation. Costs are limited to implementing state persistence per architecture and accepting that only recurrent models (TiRex-2 among the nine tested) fully satisfy accuracy, latency, and memory requirements; attention-based models still grow linearly. Can fail because most models lose accuracy beyond their trained context length, so long histories may not improve forecasts and accuracy retention must be validated on the target data before deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ANOR: Scaling Sparse Attention with a GPU-PNM Computing Hierarchy
item.description: ANOR replaces PNM-centric sparse-attention execution, in which the near-memory device computes most of the attention and becomes the bottleneck, with a GPU-centric tiering scheme: the GPU serves attention from a cache of recently selected KV entries, the CXL-PNM device handles only cache misses, and a bounded update policy plus an Early Streaming Buffer limit link traffic and redundant DRAM reads. Its costs are the need for CXL-PNM hardware, added system complexity across two compute tiers, GPU memory reserved for the KV selection cache, and an adaptive cache-factor mechanism that trades hit ratio against batch size under varying load. It can fail if the workload lacks the selection locality the GPU cache depends on, if miss rates exceed what the low-bandwidth PNM tier can absorb, or if CXL link saturation negates the decoupling of cache updates from decode execution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CGSpec: Consistency-Guided Speculative Decoding with Overlap-Aware Verification Scheduling for Edge-Cloud Inference
item.description: CGSpec replaces standard collaborative speculative decoding with static speculative budgets and naive shared-verifier scheduling by adding divergence-guided adaptive budgets, nomination-and-competition tree construction, and overlap-aware request scheduling. It costs additional verifier-side bookkeeping, client return-time estimation, and coordination logic between edge drafters and the cloud verifier. It can fail when divergence estimates misjudge draft-target agreement, when network heterogeneity invalidates return-time predictions, or in single-client deployments where the scheduling gains do not materialize. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
item.description: The study replaces intuition about guard layers and model choice with a scripted mistake library (22 canonical errors) and engine-native recovery drills across 12 engines and permission/recovery arms, showing damage is governed mainly by engine permissions and undo capability rather than the model. It costs nothing to adopt as knowledge, but operationalizing it means enforcing least-privilege credentials, tested backups, and engine-specific recovery procedures rather than relying on a guard layer whose benefit was not consistently supported. Its conclusions can fail to transfer because the post-hoc analyses (S1-S13) are exploratory and uncorrected, the preregistered outcome and original-row loss disagree about the guard layer on four engines, and one hypothesis was uninformative because agents never found the credential. 0 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
item.description: Automated LLM-as-context-engineer (LCE) methods replace manual prompt and instruction engineering by having the LLM distill generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trial trajectories. Their cost is additional offline generation over trials plus longer engineered contexts at inference, adding latency and token spend. The paper shows these methods fail when failure modes in reasoning trajectories are diverse (gains correlate negatively with failure-mode diversity, r=-0.5), do not reliably beat chain-of-thought, and do not consistently improve with more parameters or iterations, so adopting them in production is not supported by this evidence. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: sudo L7: Can Coding Agents Act Like Staff Engineers?
item.description: sudo L7 replaces ad hoc or test-pass-only evaluation of coding agents with 60 staff-engineer-authored tasks graded against 1,287 hidden atomic rubric criteria spanning eight behavioral dimensions, including truthful reporting and risk flagging. Adopting it costs nothing in infrastructure since results are on a public leaderboard, but replicating the grading methodology internally requires an agentic grader that reads transcripts, runs code, and treats test output as evidence, which adds evaluation pipeline complexity. It can fail as a selection tool because tasks are built around prior frontier-model failures in mostly private codebases, so scores may not transfer to the reader's domain, and model grader agreement with humans is only 85-86%, leaving roughly one in seven criterion verdicts unreliable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DelayOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation from a Synchronous Teacher for Real-time Asynchronous Policies
item.description: DelayOPSD replaces naive asynchronous execution of flow-based VLA policies (or training on expert demonstrations alone) by distilling a synchronous teacher, derived from the same policy with current observations, into a delayed student on the student's own rollouts, matching the teacher throughout the denoising process. It costs an additional rollout-generation and fine-tuning phase with a teacher forward pass per delayed step, but adds no modules or latency at deployment. It can fail if on-policy rollouts are expensive or unsafe to collect, if the teacher's own synchronous behavior is already weak, or if the delay regime in production exceeds the delay trained for. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
item.description: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning replaces text-level LLM judges and isolated tool-call checks as the reward source for agent training, instead supervising GRPO with deterministic verification of workspace state transitions, workflow ordering, and side effects, gated by hard zero reward on critical violations. It costs an isolated sandbox per episode that snapshots state around every tool call, a deterministic verifier, 1,000 verifiable training instances, an evidence-grounded judge for saved artifacts, and full online RL training of a 27B model, all of which exceed constrained single-GPU infrastructure. After adoption it can fail when the verifier's notion of a critical violation is incomplete or mis-specified, since reward hacking shifts to whatever state properties the verifier does not audit, and gains may not transfer beyond the 11 educational categories and 16 native tools used for training. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Quantizing Diffusion LLMs under Parallel Decoding: Commitment Risk and the Parallelism Tax
item.description: DECAL replaces standard layer-wise W4A4 post-training calibration (performed under fixed-step samplers) with commitment-risk-reweighted calibration measured on the deployed cached parallel decoder, plus an argmax-preserving commit temperature that recovers the extra forward passes quantization causes. It costs an offline commitment-risk measurement on the deployed decoder and a small change to the commit rule; memory footprint stays at W4A4 and no retraining is required. It can fail if the production decoder configuration drifts from the one used for calibration, if the model is not a dLLM served with threshold-based parallel decoding (making the method inapplicable), or if forced-commitment behavior on the reader's tasks differs from LLaDA/Dream benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentBouncer: Defending Software Engineering Agents via Dynamic System-Call Mediation
item.description: AgentBouncer replaces prompt- and trajectory-level defenses, which inspect only the initial prompt and tool-call sequence, with an LLM arbiter that mediates the actual system calls an agent triggers, gated by preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching. It costs about 47 seconds and USD 0.0036 per benign task, plus the engineering effort of integrating a syscall-interception layer into the agent's tool execution path. It can fail against attacks outside its evaluated four vectors, through arbiter misjudgment of necessity or safety on novel tasks, and if cache hits silently propagate an incorrect prior allow/deny decision. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents
item.description: The defense replaces the common pattern where provider, gateway, guard, and executor each independently parse the same raw tool-call bytes with a single parse (including JSON embedded in string arguments), projection onto the approved schema, and a canonical call sealed with its call ID that the executor uses directly. Cost is modest implementation complexity in the agent pipeline and the loss of any implicit flexibility from tolerating parser-ambiguous input; latency and memory overhead are negligible. It fails if any component bypasses the canonical representation, if schemas are too permissive (e.g., extra fields a malicious server adds that the model fills with user data), or if non-JSON channels are added later without the same treatment. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Uncovering the Tells: Efficient Black-Box Audits for LLM Data Contamination
item.description: The method replaces full-sequence sampling and uniform-position sampling heuristics for black-box training-data contamination audits with a generation-based framework that targets the few highly informative tokens carrying the membership signal. It costs implementation complexity for the token-targeting policy and still incurs per-query API inference expense, though roughly 3x less than uniform sampling. It can fail when the sparsity assumption does not hold for a given model or dataset, and results on closed frontier models remain exploratory, so contamination findings may be inconclusive or non-actionable. 0 independent implementations, 6 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity
item.description: MTL-MHOL replaces single-task CVR models that handle delayed conversions or data sparsity separately (e.g., plain ESMM or importance-weighting baselines) with a unified time-bucketing plus multi-task auxiliary-learning framework that wraps an existing backbone such as MLP or DeepFM. It costs additional pipeline complexity: maintaining time buckets, training an auxiliary task, and online-learning updates, though compute per se is modest and fits a single small GPU or even CPU-class training. It can fail if conversion-delay distributions drift, if the auxiliary task is poorly correlated with the conversion target, or if the proprietary-dataset gains do not transfer to the reader's traffic, since evidence is limited to one private dataset and Criteo. 0 independent implementations, 33 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
item.description: This replaces one-time scalar judge calibration applied uniformly across agents with per-agent error correction via augmented inverse-probability weighting over randomly audited trajectories, plus anytime-valid e-process monitoring. It costs an ongoing human audit budget (hundreds to thousands of sampled trajectory labels), added estimation complexity, and yields only bounds or rank sets when calibration support is insufficient. It can fail when the audit sampling design lacks support over the target trajectory distribution, when the judge dependence exceeds justified sensitivity bounds, or when the comparison target drifts during adaptive auditing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
item.description: IntentFlow replaces argument-level provenance-only mediation (or CaMeL-style capability checks) with a mediation layer that validates each authority-bearing tool argument against an explicit intent contract plus a provenance policy, without modifying the planner. It costs the engineering of per-tool intent contracts and provenance policies, an added check in the tool-call path, and dependency on intent/injection oracles whose real-world equivalents must be built and maintained. It can fail by residual attacks on content or payload fields (all 24 remaining successes were of this type), by over-blocking hard benign tasks (4 of 50), and wherever intent cannot be specified precisely enough to distinguish authorized from trusted-but-unrequested arguments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
item.description: GameDojo replaces ad hoc or non-interactive agent evaluations with a controlled benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games, plus 600 hours of gameplay trajectories for training and evaluation. Adoption costs include engineering effort to reconstruct and run the environments, compute for real-time rollouts, and, if used for training, fine-tuning a 4B model on the trajectory data. It can fail as a proxy: gains on game bosses may not transfer to business tasks, and models can overfit the benchmark without improving general interactive competence. 0 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference
item.description: Doc-to-LoRA replaces repeated in-context processing of memory documents by compiling them into low-rank adapters that are merged into the model, eliminating per-query document tokens. It costs answer accuracy: D2L loses to in-context learning on Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B, interference grows with bank size, and on PersonaMem-v2 it only approaches consolidated text memory when retrieved episodes remain as text, yielding modest token savings and hardware-dependent throughput gains. After adoption, multi-document banks can fail through cross-document interference and unreliable question-answer attribution, where answers to one question are contaminated by other questions or passages, and errors accumulate across layers in ways trained readers do not resolve. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.
